messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Apr 2029 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Weekly: Capacity Scenarios & Burst Eligibility for Q2 Deals

Team,

Attached are three scenario slides (low / base / upside) for Aurora Health (DEAL-7834). Sam on Aurora ops asked for clarity on whether they qualify for burst slots vs needing a dedicated pool reservation if they commit to 12 months. Quick context: their expected steady-state token throughput is ~180M tokens/day in the base scenario, with spikes to ~420M on clinical-reporting days.

Please review the following before tomorrow’s 9am Ops+Sales standup: 
- Confirm minimum reserved GPU weeks required for the base scenario (assume 8xA100-equivalent GPUs per reserved pool).
- Identify how much burst capacity we can safely promise (both absolute GPUs and duration) without violating other reserved SLAs.
- Flag any procurement/finance gating items (credits, contract language) that would delay a firm commit.

Attachments: 2029Q2_pipeline_scenarios.xlsx (tabbed by scenario), burst_eligibility_matrix.pdf

Next steps: Jordan, can you pull the latest reserved slot utilization vs committed deals and paste a short summary in the thread? Karthik, do you have a quick note on buffer thresholds for the dedicated pools? Marcus/Laura, any finance constraints to call out if we push a multi-month reserved ask?

Thanks,
Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Sales Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Apr 2029 16:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Weekly: Capacity Scenarios & Burst Eligibility for Q2 Deals

Neha — quick summary from Sales + pipeline:
- Current committed reserved slots (all customers): 312 A100-equivalent GPUs (normalized). Average utilization last 30 days: 78%.
- Upcoming near-term reserved commitments (prob >70% within 30 days): 38 GPUs cumulative across three deals (incl. 12 GPUs we expect to convert this week).
- Headroom before we hit 90% utilization: ~22 GPUs (normalized).

For Aurora (DEAL-7834): base -> requires 8 GPUs reserved to meet latency SLOs; upside -> 16 GPUs reserved if they convert to full feature set and 24/7 ingest. Burst ask they made (additional 12 GPUs for 6 hours/day on peak days): that translates to ~1.2k GPU-hours/month at current cadence.

I'll paste the HubSpot link for the latest close probability in the standup. If we commit any dedicated pool to Aurora, we should scope an isolated pool (8 GPUs) with a pre-configured burst policy — but we need infra confirmation that such a pool won't erode our buffer for other qualified deals.

-Jordan
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Apr 2029 07:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Weekly: Capacity Scenarios & Burst Eligibility for Q2 Deals

Thanks for the details — technical notes and constraints: 

1) Current pool configuration: we have three shared reserved pools (44 / 128 / 140 GPU normalized buckets). The small pool (44) is at 71% avg utilization; medium at 83%; large at 82%.

2) Burst eligibility calc: given our SLAs and fair-share policies, we can safely offer Aurora bursts up to 10 GPUs for short windows (<= 8 hours) provided we define preemption priorities and require a modest buffer (we maintain a 10% safety margin on each pool). If Aurora needs consistent 6+ hours/day bursts multiple times per week, they cross into needing dedicated reservation for predictable cost and latency.

3) Suggested action: offer a hybrid: 8 GPU dedicated minimum pool for base SLA + a negotiated burst allowance up to 10 GPUs for peak days (up to 4 days/month) with costs defined per-GB/HR of usage. This preserves our ability to honor higher-priority enterprise commitments.

4) Timeline & ops: we can stand up the dedicated 8-GPU pool within 7 business days after contract signature and KMS keys provisioned. If procurement needs SOC2 evidence or additional compliance attestation, that will add ~3-5 business days.

Attachment: burst_eligibility_matrix.pdf (same as Neha’s; I exported infra constraints into last tab).

-Karthik
From: Sam Lee <sam.lee@aurorahealth.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@aurorahealth.ai
Date: Tue, 30 Apr 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Weekly: Capacity Scenarios & Burst Eligibility for Q2 Deals

Thanks, Neha/Jordan/Karthik — this is helpful context. A few clarifying points from Aurora ops and procurement: 

- We can commit to the 12-month term if Redwood can guarantee the 8-GPU dedicated unit for base with the burst allowance you propose (10 GPUs, preemptible no earlier than 6 hours after request).
- Procurement requests a single-line item in the SOW that lists the dedicated pool (8x A100-equivalent), burst hourly rate, and the expected RTO (time to provision additional GPUs). Can you send a short SOW snippet we can attach to purchase order?
- Security/compliance: we requested the SOC2 attestation last week; if you can share the signed report or the customer SOC2 extract link, that will speed our internal approval.

We'd like to keep the procurement process moving this week; if you can provide the SOW snippet + SOC2 link, we’ll aim to return a signed PO by next Wed.

Best,
Sam Lee
Head of Machine Ops, Aurora Health
